content_units: Kyoto 5-Day Trip Snapshot

For   2 adults   in   Kyoto   from   2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14  , a   120,000 JPY   ground budget is workable for a   moderate-paced   trip if you prioritize temple/garden entry, local trains/buses, casual meals, and one carefully chosen day trip. This plan keeps each day to   no more than 3 major activities   and focuses on   temples, tea, gardens, and quieter neighborhoods  .
Budget-Fit Itinerary by Day
Day 1: Southern Higashiyama Arrival Walk
- Morning: Start at   Kiyomizu-dera   early to enjoy the temple grounds before peak crowds.
- Afternoon: Walk the quieter lanes of   Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka, and Maruyama Park  , then continue toward   Kodai-ji   for garden and bamboo grove atmosphere.
- Dinner: Have a relaxed   kaiseki-style lunch set or tofu dinner   in Higashiyama.
Area map
Day 2: Arashiyama Temples and Garden Calm
- Morning: Visit   Tenryu-ji   and its garden, then take a short walk through the   Arashiyama bamboo grove   before it gets busy.
- Afternoon: Explore the quieter   Okochi Sanso Garden   or walk the riverside and backstreets west of the main bamboo path.
- Dinner: Try a   tea house dessert stop   and simple soba or yudofu near Arashiyama Station.
Arashiyama info
Day 3: Uji Day Trip for Tea and Byodo-in
- Morning: Take the train to   Uji   for   Byodo-in Temple   and its museum.
- Afternoon: Visit a   tea shop/cafe for matcha tasting   and walk the river area at a slow pace.
- Dinner: Return to Kyoto for an easy dinner near your hotel or Kyoto Station.
Uji guide
Day 4: Northern Kyoto Quiet Temples
- Morning: Visit   Ginkaku-ji   and stroll the start of the   Philosopher’s Path  .
- Afternoon: Continue slowly to   Honen-in   or   Nanzen-ji   depending on energy; both suit a quiet temple-and-garden day.
- Dinner: Eat in the   Okazaki   or   Demachiyanagi   area for a calmer evening than central Kawaramachi.
Northern Kyoto
Day 5: Imperial Kyoto and Tea Finish
- Morning: Walk through   Kyoto Gyoen National Garden / Kyoto Imperial Palace Park   for a spacious, calm final morning.
- Afternoon: Choose one final stop:   Shosei-en Garden   if staying near Kyoto Station, or a formal   tea experience   in central Kyoto.
- Dinner: Finish with a special but budget-aware dinner in   Pontocho area side streets   or a quiet neighborhood restaurant.
City guide
Cost Breakdown Table
Category   Estimated Cost (JPY)   Notes
Local transport   12,000   IC card/top-ups for 2 adults across 5 days, including Uji day trip
Temple/garden admissions   16,000   Mix of major temples and 1-2 paid gardens for 2 adults
Tea experiences   10,000   One nice matcha tasting or tea house visit for 2
Lunches   20,000   About 2,000 per meal for 2 on most days
Dinners   32,000   About 5,500-7,000 for 2 on 4 regular nights plus 1 nicer meal
Snacks/cafes   8,000   Sweets, coffee, tea breaks
Contingency   22,000   Souvenirs, extra entry, weather adjustments
Total       120,000     Fits your stated cap
Why This Plan Fits Your Priorities
-   Temples and gardens first:   Kiyomizu-dera, Kodai-ji, Tenryu-ji, Byodo-in, Ginkaku-ji, and Kyoto Gyoen match your interests well.
-   Quiet neighborhoods:   Southern Higashiyama early, Arashiyama side lanes, Uji riverside, Philosopher’s Path area, and Imperial Park all feel calmer than downtown shopping districts.
-   Moderate pace:   Each day has   2-3 major activities max  , with built-in walking time and tea breaks.
-   Walking + trains:   All days work well with   rail + short local transit + on-foot exploration  .
-   One day trip maximum:   Only   Uji   is included, and it is easy, short, and highly aligned with your tea interest.

Trip Notes for April Timing
- Mid-April is often excellent for   spring gardens and fresh greenery  , though peak cherry blossom may be fading depending on the year.
- Start temple areas   early morning   whenever possible to keep the experience quieter.
- If rain is forecast, swap in   Nanzen-ji, Shosei-en, or tea houses   since they still work well in light rain.
